subject: lavaGolem
pitch:
Category: Monster.
Subject: lava golem of basalt plates and molten seams.
Style: Genshin Impact.
reasoning:
I'm planning out a TypeScript module to build a lava golem styled after Genshin Impact monsters, aiming for a sizable but structurally safe design with around 250 parts and multiple textures, drawing inspiration from creatures like Pyro Hypostasis or Ruin Guards.

The design concept is a dark basalt golem with glowing orange cracks, a glowing chest core, heavy grounded legs, large fisted arms, a small head with a separate jaw, obsidian back spikes trimmed in fire, and a pyro emblem, all rendered in clean cel-shaded Genshin style with gold trim and glow effects. I'm sketching the skeleton structure -- a hips root with spine chains up to the head, leg chains through hip/knee/ankle joints, arm chains through shoulder/elbow/wrist into finger digits, plus jaw and back crystal attachments -- while keeping the builder API calls (joints, chains, sweeps, parts) simple and safe since I can't test the code directly.

Now I'm working out how to layer the body: an inner molten glowing core built from flat-colored sweeps and capsule shapes, surrounded by black basalt plates with gaps that reveal the glow underneath, using low-segment flat-faceted boxes and cylinders for the plating and mottled dark paint textures with explicit shadow tones for the stone surfaces.

I'm picking the color palette next—dark basalt tones in violet-gray, lava oranges and deep reds for the glow, plus some cream or ash accents for contrast, keeping flat colors under the limit since paints don't count against it.

Now I'm planning the texture work: a glowing angular eye motif decaled onto the head surface with a hot yellow slit center, and separate crack textures for the plates to sell the molten lava-under-stone look.

I'm also sketching out a pyro emblem for the chest core, flame-card textures for crest and shoulder fire licks, and rune-band decals for the forearms—landing on roughly five textures plus paints to stay within budget. Then I move into blocking out the skeleton, aiming for a total height around 3.4 meters.

For the thick golem-style legs, I'm placing hip, knee, and ankle points for each side and setting up the chain with named joints so the ankle tip aligns along the end tangent, using three points per leg to create a two-span chain down to the foot blocks.

I'm deciding to build the legs as stacked plate segments — a smooth catmull-swept lava-dark core sweep (radius ~0.26) representing molten inner material, overlaid with flat basalt armor boxes for the rigid exterior look, keeping the thighs noticeably thick.

For the plate construction itself, I'm defining a helper that extrudes outlines into slabs with optional bevels, oriented so front-facing plates run width along X and thickness along Z, and planning to use six-sided cylinders to get the iconic hexagonal basalt column shapes for spikes and armor details.

Now I'm sketching out the body's joint hierarchy in model space—pelvis at the hip joint, then a spine chain running up through chest to neck base, with hips as the root and spine joints parented off it.

Next I'm positioning the neck and head above the shoulders, keeping the golem's head small and compact, with a short neck chain parented to the spine tip and the head as the chain's terminal joint.

Still defining joint placements...

Adding a flat skull base with brow ridge, horn columns, and a lower jaw box, plus a glowing lava cavity between upper and lower jaws for the mouth.

I'm adding small cone teeth with a cream angular shape, positioning the jaw hinge at the back of the skull, and placing angular glowing eye slits as a decal on the front face of the skull -- being careful to avoid negative scale mirroring since it flips winding order, so I'll need another way to make the eyes asymmetrical left versus right.

I'm also planning a crest of flame-textured cards along the back of the head and neck for a fiery glow, and deciding to keep embers minimal and only attached near the shoulders rather than freely floating, since the subject itself should carry all the detail.

For the torso, I'm sweeping a loft from hips to chest along the spine bone chain with an elliptical radius profile, glowing with a deep lava color, then layering armor: paired angled pectoral plates with a central open window revealing a glowing Pyro core, three stacked overlapping abdominal plates with visible lava gaps, a dorsal back plate with hex-column spikes, and rib plates on the sides. I'm now nailing down concrete sizes and coordinates for the spine sweep path.

Writing plate geometry helper...

Working out the tilt math for the thickness axis cross product, I'm designing a helper function that builds a tapered plate with configurable tilt, taper, yaw, color, and thickness, so pecs and similar flat shapes can lean at the right angle with proper surface normals.

For the actual rotation computation, I'll apply pitch and yaw rotations to base x/y vectors using Euler rotation methods rather than lookAt or setFromUnitVectors, which are off-limits. For extrusion, I'm checking whether outline polygons need consistent winding and confirming that corner smoothing stays at zero so edges stay sharp by default, and noting how paint/mottle functions receive their surface vectors. For hex columns I'll use a six-sided cylinder geometry with flat shading.

Now I'm working out the arm rig: shoulder-elbow-wrist joint positions with arms hanging slightly outward and large fists near the knees, then planning finger chains as five digits per hand with two joints each, built from small hexagonal column segments with knuckle caps, keeping the total joint count comfortably under the 160 limit while fingers splay slightly downward in the rest pose.

Writing the arm chain code...

For the molten core under armor, I'm thinking hex-column bundles wrapping the upper arm, with a chunkier gauntlet and blocky fist at the wrist for that heavy golem look. I want to keep the design choices simple enough to stay manageable in code.

For each shoulder I'm planning stacked hexagonal plates with lava seams and outward-facing spikes, attached at the shoulder joint, plus a helper function that wraps flat plates radially around a limb segment so I can reuse it for both arms.

Still writing wrap helper logic...

For a hex ring with n=6 plates, I'm computing the apothem radius and plate width using the tangent of 30°, with a slight overlap gap to let lava glow show through the seams between plates and ring segments. I'm also considering reusing this wrapping approach for limbs and the torso, since the abdomen can still use a cylindrical wrap even though it's not a true cylinder.

Now I'm working out the hand geometry: a palm block positioned below the wrist, with four finger chains and a thumb extending downward, each finger made of shrinking segments and spaced by x-offsets across the palm width, oriented so the palms face inward toward the body.

Adding obsidian spike tips to fingers and tallying up joint counts across spine, neck, head, legs, arms, and fingers.

Now I'm working out leg joint placement with hip, knee, and ankle positions, tapering thigh and shin radii for an armored look, and blocking out a chunky foot shape at the ankle.

For the pelvis, I'm thinking through hip plates with hanging tasset-like trapezoids and a simple glowing belt loop, keeping the geometry lightweight rather than overcomplicating with full digit chains for toes.

For the Genshin-inspired golem aesthetic, I'm settling on a basalt dark violet palette with gold trim rings (#e8b84a/#f2c14e) on belt, shoulder, and bracer edges, plus a Pyro emblem accent, with lava orange and ember red highlights throughout.

I'm placing the chest core at the torso front with a glowing hot yellow-orange sphere nested inside a hex-plate ring frame, flanked by angled pec plates, and planning texture layers for the emblem, cracks, and surface detail.

Still writing SVG code...

For placing crack decals onto the plate surfaces, I'm thinking through using a decal helper that projects the texture at a given position and direction with set size, then applying a glow effect to the resulting part. I need to account for tilted plates affecting the projection angle, and consider what happens if the decal grid extends beyond the plate's edges.

Instead, I'm leaning toward a more deterministic approach: using simple plane geometry parts offset slightly from each plate's surface, oriented along the plate's own normal and up vector, which avoids projection risk entirely for both flat and tilted plates. I'll have my plate-generating function return the part along with its center, normal, and up vector so a helper can position the crack plane correctly and apply the glow.

Now I'm working through how the plane's rotation axis follows the "up" direction, confirming that the textured face points outward along the plate's normal, and computing that normal by crossing the plate's local x and y vectors after rotation is applied, same logic for the eye plane on the skull.

Writing paint and color definitions...

I'm checking how cel shading works with mottle nested inside, confirming the shadow color parameter is typed correctly and each distinct paint adds to the painted area count without issue.

For wear details, I'm considering a scorched gradient on the lower legs and feet, giving them an ember-red underglow near the ground with dark ashy tones at the very bottom.

Now I'm working out the head proportions—placing the head center forward and low against hunched shoulders, with the skull, neck, and horns stacking up to a total figure height around 3.4 units.

Adding skull, brow, cheek, and horn geometry...

Eye planes go at the sides of the face, with a small glowing octahedron gem at the brow center for a forehead jewel. I'm adding glowing vent slits near the cheeks for the mouth glow, and planning a dorsal flame crest made of card meshes anchored to the spine joint, sized and leaned appropriately before applying the glow effect to them.

For the head, I'm placing flame tufts near the rear using offset frames bound to the head bone, plus floating shoulder flames in a Pyro style, using cross-faced cards so the flame texture reads from any angle with upward growth along the frame axis. For the back, I'm planning two large angled dorsal plates plus five hex-column spikes along the spine with lava-glow cuts at their bases, along with hex-column vent clusters topped with flame cards on the shoulders. I'm also sketching glowing seam strips between torso plates and multiple rows of abdomen plates with lava visible through the gaps, working out vertical placement for the chest core.

Now I'm working out precise vertical and radial positioning: hips at y=1.45, a waist belt at 1.55, two abdomen plate rows around y=1.7–1.9 with center-plus-angled-side plates, then a chest region from about 2.08 to 2.55 with a core, pecs, and collar, following a spine curve that bows forward toward the chest, and figuring out how far forward the core should sit based on the torso's elliptical cross-section.

I'm placing the core sphere at the chest center and pushing it slightly forward of the chest plates, then checking that the pec placement leaves enough gap between them for the core and emblem to fit without overlapping, adjusting the pec x-offset and width until the gap is wide enough for a flattened glowing disc core with an emblem plane floating just in front of its surface.

Now I'm plotting the arm chain, placing shoulders, elbows, wrists, and fists so the arm swing clears the torso and legs, making sure fist height sits near the knee without colliding with leg geometry, and sanity-checking overall body width and height come out to a believable 3.4m golem scale.

Adding armor wraps and joint details...

Now I'm working out the legs similarly—thigh wrap radius around 0.33 down to the knee, shin wrap slightly narrower, with a hex knee cap and forward spike, then the foot. I'm also settling on treating the hex ring radius as the center radius for the wrap boxes, so the outer face sits at rad plus half the thickness.

I'm computing the hex box width from the apothem using the tangent of 30 degrees, then adjusting for thickness so the corners line up cleanly. I'm also setting up an aim helper that builds local axes from a direction vector and an "up" lean, returning a quaternion for orienting each part, and I'm adding a glow effect with higher strength for the lava look, noting that leg seams will show gaps since the wraps only cover part of the limb. For the torso's inner sweep, I'm defining a radius function along the spine chain that gradually widens from about 0.5 to 0.7.

Now I'm widening the pelvis area with a basalt-textured hip block plus a glow strip, attaching parts to the hips joint, and adding dorsal column cylinders and angled back plates along the spine for a rugged rear silhouette. I'm also shaping cone-based teeth that point downward for the upper jaw and upward for the lower, and assigning rig roles like spine, neck, head, and jaw to the corresponding joints.

I'm defining joint hierarchy with explicit parent-child relationships starting from the hips root, setting direction and aim vectors for the head and jaw joints, and establishing unique naming patterns for finger bones and joint chains per side before laying out the wrist and palm block positions.

Working out finger coordinates...

Still defining finger geometry...
